primitives.name: Measure-Preserving Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: Every separable, non atomic, normalized measure algebra (S,μ) is isomorphic to the measure algebra (T,v) of the unit interval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'Separable, nonatomic measure algebra', 'μ': 'Normalized measure on S', 'T': 'Unit interval', 'v': 'Lebesgue measure on T'}
primitives.assumptions: S is separable, non-atomic, and normalized; T is the unit interval with Lebesgue measure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S lacks separability or contains atoms, the isomorphism fails.

layer2.mapping: Maps abstract measure algebras to concrete interval measures for computational tractability.
layer2.telemetry: Verification via density of finite unions of intervals.

These partitions are shown to be decreasing and dense, leading to the conclusion that limn |Pn| = 0. This convergence enables a measure-preserving map T from s(μ) to J(v), where J(v) represents the space of intervals with Lebesgue measure. The isomorphism between (S,μ) and (T,v) is established by constructing a sequence of partitions {Qn} on the unit interval such that each element of Pn maps to a corresponding interval in Qn with equal measure. This construction ensures that any measurable set in S can be represented as a union of intervals in T, preserving both structure and measure. The failure mode occurs when the underlying space lacks separability or contains atoms, breaking the bijection required for the isomorphism.
